title: Skills and routing
blurb: Priority math, bullseye, routing attributes, and the Personal Connection exception.

lessons.title: Priority and acceleration
lessons.summary: Overall priority is (Time × Acceleration) + Initial Priority, capped by Maximum Priority. The published three-minute example lands on 7.

p: The static delivery page says acceleration is how fast priority rises. The default is 1. The minimum is 0. Maximum priority caps the result. For every minute in queue, priority increases by the acceleration value. With acceleration 1, thirty seconds adds 0.5.
Example: initial 4, acceleration 1, three minutes, priority 7. The formula line is Overall Priority = (Time × Acceleration) + Initial Priority.

cites.title: Configure Priority for a Skill for Static Delivery

sections.h: A sentence that does not match
p: The same page says a skill with initial 1 and acceleration 5 overtakes a skill with initial 3 and acceleration 1 after one minute, reaching 6. That part matches the formula: (1 × 5) + 1 = 6.
It also says the second skill starts at priority 4. The formula at time zero is 3. This lab teaches the formula and the three-minute example, and marks the 'starts at 4' sentence as uncertain.

lessons.title: Bullseye with proficiency
lessons.summary: Bullseye adds and removes agents by proficiency, routing attributes, or both. COUNTAGENTS, GETQUEUE, REQAGENT, and UpdateContact can carry it.

p: Bullseye can use skill proficiency, routing attributes, or both. Proficiency is assigned with the skill. Attributes are custom traits, such as a language, that narrow or widen the same skill's pool.
The page's key facts: assign proficiency on the user profile or the skill record, and configure bullseye on COUNTAGENTS, GETQUEUE, REQAGENT, and UpdateContact.
If you use WFM, read that product's guidance first. CXone WFM users are pointed at the online help. IEX users are pointed at the Distribution Rules Guide.
A window that never widens protects quality and misses the service target. A window that starts at 1–20 does not prefer anyone. Both are configuration choices, not platform bugs.

lessons.title: Personal Connection acceleration is zero
lessons.summary: Personal Connection skills set acceleration to 0 because there is no queue of contacts. Initial priority still matters for blending. Dialing by proficiency is a separate pair of checkboxes.

p: The static delivery page says: for Personal Connection skills, set acceleration to 0 because there is no queue of contacts. You can still set initial priority so one skill is considered ahead of another when blending.

The same page notes an Outbound Engagement (SmartReach) skill where initial priority is, at the time of that writing, the only available priority setting. Do not assume every outbound product has the same three fields.

cites.title: Configure Priority for a Skill for Static Delivery

p: Personal Connection can weight distribution by agent wait, simultaneous calls, and optionally proficiency. Enable Dialing by Proficiency on the business unit, under ACD Configuration > Business Units, Outbound Strategies. Then enable it on the skill's Parameters tab, General Pacing Settings.
The page says you may change the default weights but should consult your account representative before you do. This lab does not publish replacement weights.

faults.title: Outbound starves or never yields
faults.symptom: A PC skill was given acceleration 5 'so it would compete,' and inbound contacts jump the moment any PC activity exists, or the reverse complaint appears after someone zeroes an inbound skill.
faults.cause: The page's rule is the opposite: PC at 0, inbound aging with its own acceleration, rank them with initial priority.
faults.fix: Set PC acceleration to 0 and give inbound a real acceleration. Adjust initial priorities for the blend you want.

lessons.title: Routing attributes
lessons.summary: Attributes are custom traits on agents. The bullseye page uses language as the example beside proficiency. They are not skills, and they are not OAuth scopes.
objectives: Define an attribute with the page's words
Not invent the attribute admin URL

p: Marguerite uses proficiency for fiction-book knowledge and routing attributes for language. The combination is how she keeps the Classics experience specific without a separate skill for every pair.

The page says you create and assign the attributes, then configure Studio actions to use them. It does not, in the section cited here, list every property on the attribute form. Do not invent required fields.
UPDATE CONTACT DIGITAL can replace routing criteria that Reqagent set earlier. Its default routing-criteria option is Not Applicable. Proficiency high and low are still 1–20.
If you are on digital, read that action's page before you copy a voice UpdateContact property name across.

lessons.title: Blending, bullseye, and the forecast
lessons.summary: Initial priority ranks work when you blend. Bullseye changes who can take it. The forecast assumed a pool. Change one and you owe the WFM team a look.
objectives: Rank blended work with initial priority
Tell WFM when the pool changes
Use What-If rather than a silent edit

sections.h: What WFM can do about a change
p: General Forecast lets you build alternative forecasts with What-If, using the same parameters and history while you change forecast data. You can compare staffing plans. The page also says forecast data is regenerated after staffing parameters, because scheduling units that can handle the work are considered.
That is the official place to look at a different future. It is not a promise that What-If understands bullseye windows. The bullseye page still says to read the WFM guidance.
Write the routing change: new initial priorities, new windows. Then ask WFM to look at history, AHT, and the service target before the schedule is published.

CXone WFM says it supports tenants up to 10,000 agents, and that Scheduling, Forecasting, Intraday, Real-Time Adherence, Time Off, and Reporting are certified at that scale. A routing change is still a forecast change at 50 agents.

lessons.title: What this lab will not claim about delivery
lessons.summary: The simulator breaks ties by longest idle. Personal Connection documents wait time, simultaneous calls, and optional proficiency. A universal inbound tie-break is not stated on the pages cited here.
objectives: Say the classroom tie-break out loud
Refuse a fake 'always longest idle' policy

p: The proactive voice page says PC distributes calls using the agent's wait time, current simultaneous calls, and optionally proficiency. Weights are the distribution factors you should not edit casually.
That sentence is about Personal Connection. It is not a description of every inbound ACD delivery mode.
This floor's routing simulator, after priority and the proficiency window, picks the longest current idle agent. That rule is labeled in the tool. It is not a citation.
If a production question is 'who among three eligible agents gets the contact,' open the current delivery help for that skill type. Do not answer from the simulator.
